clue.text: Cheat told conundrums changing ends around

indicators.note: the two end letters of the word swap places, a minimal rearrangement

parts.note: to riddle is to speak in riddles, so having told conundrums is having riddled

explanation.surface: A con artist spins puzzling stories to wrong-foot a victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing ends around' swaps the first and last letters of RIDDLED, R and D, giving DIDDLER; nothing else moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A diddler is an informal word for a swindler, someone who cons people.

clue.text: Art style with strange decency

parts.note: Art Deco is the 1920s and 1930s design style, so the art style here is deco
rum is a dated British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An artistic movement with an unusual sense of propriety.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper, polite behaviour, a near synonym of decency.

clue.text: Footballer gets millions for nothing having letter, we hear, to go on old quiz show

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter goes on top of the footballer
the letter is spelt out as it is said

parts.note: the letter is W, which is spoken as double-u

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: Wayne Rooney is an England footballer
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A footballer wins a fortune for nothing on a vintage TV quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps one O of the footballer's name for M; 'we hear' spells the letter W as it is spoken. Double Your Money was a 1950s-60s British TV quiz show.
explanation.definitionFit: Double Your Money was a British television quiz from the 1950s and 1960s, hosted by Hughie Green.

clue.text: Improvement towards the end in heading for one side

indicators.note: the lateness word is placed at the head, before the improvement

parts.note: late means near the end
a rally is a recovery or improvement, as in share prices

explanation.surface: A team improves late on while heading to one side of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in heading' puts LATE at the head of RALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Laterally means sideways, to or from one side.

clue.text: River, Russian one, in the country

parts.note: a Russian river, the Ural, flowing from the Ural Mountains

explanation.surface: A river, a Russian one, out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian one' refers back to River: a Russian river, the Ural.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means relating to the countryside, away from towns.

clue.text: Wreckage in half of Family Fortunes

indicators.note: the fortunes word sits inside the half-word
only the first three of the six letters of Family are taken

parts.note: lots are fortunes or destinies, as in one's lot in life

explanation.surface: A TV game show half-way through collapses into a shambles.
explanation.walkthrough: Family Fortunes was a long-running British TV game show; 'half of Family' is FAM, which holds LOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is floating wreckage of a ship or its cargo.

clue.text: Poetic style produces great excitement round about Home Counties

indicators.note: the excitement word goes round the short word for concerning

parts.note: a fever pitch of excitement, a fever
re means concerning, about
the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England, SE

explanation.surface: A poetry movement generates huge excitement around the counties near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the South East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Free verse is poetry without regular metre or rhyme, a style of poetry.

clue.text: Place for refreshment that's ordinary in its present state

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
as is means unchanged, in the present state

explanation.surface: A plain refreshment spot left just as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert with water, a place to refresh oneself.

clue.text: Dog chewed up grannies' slipper

indicators.note: something chewed up is mangled into a different shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The family dog has gnawed Granny's slipper to bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed up' shuffles all fifteen letters of GRANNIES SLIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: The springer spaniel is a breed of gundog.

clue.text: Half-hearted wife journalist treated badly

indicators.note: one of the two central letters, half the heart, is dropped

parts.note: missus is an informal word for a wife
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A lukewarm wife complains that a reporter mistreated her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' removes one of the two middle S letters of MISSUS, leaving MISUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Misused means abused or mistreated, treated badly.

clue.text: Craftily creates numerous defensive tactics

indicators.note: doing something craftily means cunningly reworking it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A schemer cunningly devises many ways of protecting themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craftily' shuffles CREATES NUMEROUS, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Countermeasures are actions taken to counter a threat, which is exactly what defensive tactics are.

clue.text: Sovereign that will keep one going straight

definitions.meaning: a monarch or king who reigns over a country

definitions.text: that will keep one going straight
definitions.meaning: a measuring stick used to draw straight lines

explanation.surface: A monarch who keeps subjects on the straight and narrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a reigning monarch and the straight-edged stick for drawing lines.

clue.text: Goss worked with novel romantic numbers

indicators.note: letters worked over are kneaded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A writer called Goss produced a novel with some romance in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' shuffles GOSS together with NOVEL; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers are songs or musical pieces, and romantic ones are ballads about love.

clue.text: Historic vessel takes PM to river

parts.note: Theresa May was a British Prime Minister
crossword joke: a river is something that flows, a flower

explanation.surface: A prime minister boards an old ship bound for a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river' as FLOWER is a crossword favourite: read it as flow-er, one that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620, a famous historic ship.

clue.text: Cavalier, to support little free time after work

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
a cavalier was a mounted gentleman soldier, a knight

explanation.surface: A dashing gallant helps out with a little leisure after work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' sets KNIGHT below WEE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A weeknight is an evening from Monday to Friday, when free time comes after the working day.

clue.text: Stepped on it going round kitchen, finally getting fork out

indicators.note: the hurrying word encircles the single letter

parts.note: to step on it is to hurry, so having stepped on it is having sped

indicators.note: the last letter of kitchen is used

explanation.surface: Someone rushes round a kitchen before finally buying a fork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes N from kitchen and 'going round' puts it inside SPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To fork out is an idiom for paying money, which is to spend it.

clue.text: Heir hit gold

parts.note: a hit is a success, like a hit record
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An heir strikes it rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A successor is one who follows another in a role or title, as an heir does.

clue.text: Some famous Yorkshiremen lacking charisma

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dig at certain celebrated men from Yorkshire for being dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousy describes a timid, drab person with no presence or charm.

clue.text: Demonstrated with craft in sea

indicators.note: the cunning word sits inside the sea

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
arch means sly or crafty, done with craft

explanation.surface: Protesters show their point with boats out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with craft' suggests boats, but means cunning: ARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters who demonstrate often march, so marched is to have demonstrated in a procession.

clue.text: Drill cuts out round emergency room

indicators.note: the cutting word goes around the hospital abbreviation

parts.note: to excise is to cut something out

explanation.surface: A surgical drill cuts away near the emergency room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drill' looks like a tool in this hospital picture, but it means practice routines.
explanation.definitionFit: Drill as a noun means practice routines, the same as training exercises.

clue.text: Flats etc providing pleasant views

definitions.meaning: flats are painted theatre backdrops, part of a stage set

explanation.surface: Apartments that offer attractive outlooks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the painted stage set and an attractive natural landscape.

clue.text: Artist's distinctive design described by strange term

indicators.note: to be described is to have something drawn around you, so the outer letters circle this piece
strange letters are oddly arranged ones

parts.note: a brand is a distinctive trademark or design

explanation.surface: An artist's signature style is captured by an odd expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges TERM as REMT, and 'described by' sets BRAND inside it: REM-BRAND-T. The 's after Artist stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt was the Dutch master painter of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Greek character carrying in dosh

indicators.note: the Greek letter holds the little word within it

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man brings in some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhino and dosh are both British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old British slang for money, as is dosh.

clue.text: Group of soldiers has bad time in revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: poor means bad, of low quality

explanation.surface: An army unit suffers a rough spell during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' turns POORT around to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of soldiers, especially of cavalry or artillery.

clue.text: Avoid First Lady touring area with diamonds

indicators.note: the lady goes around the two letters as if travelling round them

parts.note: in the Bible Eve is the first woman
D is the card-playing abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Keep away from a president's wife travelling a region with her jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' looks like a president's wife but is Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to dodge or escape something, a synonym of avoid.

clue.text: County formerly seeking teachers' charter

parts.note: hunting means searching for, seeking
dons are university teachers
to charter a boat or plane is to hire it

explanation.surface: Educators looking for a founding document.
explanation.walkthrough: HUNTINGDONSHIRE was an English county, merged into Cambridgeshire in 1974, hence 'formerly'.
explanation.definitionFit: It was once an English shire, now part of Cambridgeshire, so a former county.

clue.text: Trips over in performing a study

indicators.note: the cricket letter sits inside the rearranged letters
letters performing are put through their paces in a new arrangement

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Holidays finished while someone acts out a piece of research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges A STUDY as DAYSUT, and 'in' places O inside: DAYS-O-UT.
explanation.definitionFit: Days out are excursions, short outings or jaunts, the same as trips.

clue.text: Talk about southern herb

indicators.note: the talking word wraps around the single letter

parts.note: a parley is a talk, especially between enemies

explanation.surface: A chat about a herb grown in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts S inside PARLEY: PAR-S-LEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsley is a common green culinary herb used for garnish.
